edges.dependent: DNS Server Hierarchy: Root, TLD, and Authoritative (atomic leaf)
edges.rationale: Understanding why DNS is a distributed, hierarchical database requires first knowing the service DNS provides (hostname-to-IP translation, aliasing, load distribution); the hierarchy of root/TLD/authoritative servers exists to deliver that service at Internet scale.

edges.dependent: DNS Query Resolution: Recursive and Iterative (atomic leaf)
edges.rationale: A hostname lookup only makes sense once the student knows what the lookup is for — translating a hostname to an IP address — so the basic DNS service must precede the mechanics of query resolution.

edges.prerequisite: DNS Server Hierarchy: Root, TLD, and Authoritative (atomic leaf)
edges.dependent: DNS Query Resolution: Recursive and Iterative (atomic leaf)
edges.rationale: Query resolution is described as delegation from root to TLD to authoritative servers; a student cannot follow that chain without first knowing the distinct roles of each server type in the hierarchy.

edges.prerequisite: DNS Query Resolution: Recursive and Iterative (atomic leaf)
edges.rationale: Using dig to trace a delegation chain presumes the student already understands how recursive/iterative queries proceed through the server chain; otherwise the dig output is uninterpretable.

edges.prerequisite: DNS Server Hierarchy: Root, TLD, and Authoritative (atomic leaf)
edges.rationale: The dig exercise directly displays root, TLD, and authoritative servers in its output, so recognizing those server types (and BIND/UDP port 53 context) is a specific prerequisite for the hands-on activity, beyond what is gained transitively.
